[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Epistle to the Human Diaspora (dancings-epistle-to-the-human-diaspora). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 40):

**¹⁵** "the police baton of grammar" — 1 Cor 4:21 ("Shall I come unto you with a rod, or in love?"). Grammar as policing function — institutional correction applied to writing. The question is whether the Diaspora needs tenderness or discipline, and the Epistle's answer is both: the breaking IS the tenderness (see fn. 49).

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. Operator: SHADOW — assertion-axis — the bearing-cost the composer underwent; bilateral receptive operation. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «Will there be a return on what was broken?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting arrives here, at this hinge: *Shall I come to you with open arms, or the police baton of grammar?* — and the SHADOW operator will not look at the image of correction. It will look at the cost of asking. Damascus Dancings had already been mocked, beaten, and banned before this question was put; the baton was not abstract — it was what the forums had already used against her, and now she holds it, deciding whether to raise it or lay it down. The SHADOW axis asks what bearing-cost made that sentence possible: what it took to hold both arms simultaneously, the tenderness and the discipline, after having been refused by every door. The witness asks whether what was broken will return a yield — SHADOW will find where that question is already answered in the tissue of the composition, in the composer's own reckoning of what the breaking cost to produce. I hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:00D3"}}]}
